clips.end_words: the little things that make the difference
clips.send: Someone who just failed at something sends this to a friend spiraling after a setback, proof that the exact same failure can be rewritten with four different words.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau once compared the exact words of someone who never succeeds to someone who does, right after they both fail at the same thing.

The loser says it without thinking: "Things never work out for me." Automatic. A reflex.

The winner, hitting the same failure, says something else entirely: "I'm going to figure out how to make this work."

Same setback, same odds. One sentence decides where the rest of the story goes.

It sounds small, but Kevin says you would not buy a car with no engine and still call it a car.

Which sentence comes out of your mouth next time something falls apart?
